world.title: Leaked files expose Deutsche Bank control failures, trigger German scrutiny
world.summary: An international investigation published Nov. 17, based on more than 15 million leaked Deutsche Bank records, described years of alleged failures in the lender’s anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls. The documents cover dealings with Russian clients, Jeffrey Epstein and President Donald Trump. A separate review
world.content: An international investigation published Nov. 17, based on more than 15 million leaked Deutsche Bank records, described years of alleged failures in the lender’s anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls. The documents cover dealings with Russian clients, Jeffrey Epstein and President Donald Trump. A separate review of the bank’s Colombian correspondent-banking business found it processed more than €20 billion for the country’s largest banks while filing fewer than 10 suspicious-activity reports in one year. In the Colombian review, external monitors appointed by U.S. authorities criticized delays in investigating missed alerts. The bank later filed at least 294 reports about transactions identified in the review. Deutsche Bank said the matters were historical and pointed to €7 billion invested in controls from 2019 to 2025. German Finance Minister and Vice Chancellor Lars Klingbeil called for full transparency and said authorities should investigate and act where necessary. Germany’s financial regulator BaFin granted the bank another extension last month to improve systems to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
world.image_alt: Leaked files expose Deutsche Bank control failures, trigger German scrutiny

world.title: Pakistani man receives 27-year sentence for plot targeting Trump
world.summary: A federal judge in Brooklyn sentenced Pakistani national Asif Merchant to 330 months in prison on Nov. 17 for plotting to hire assassins to kill President Donald Trump and other U.S. political figures, the Justice Department said. A jury convicted Merchant in March 2026 of attempting transnational terrorism and murder
world.content: A federal judge in Brooklyn sentenced Pakistani national Asif Merchant to 330 months in prison on Nov. 17 for plotting to hire assassins to kill President Donald Trump and other U.S. political figures, the Justice Department said. A jury convicted Merchant in March 2026 of attempting transnational terrorism and murder for hire. Prosecutors said the plot sought revenge for the January 2020 U.S. drone strike that killed Iranian commander Qassem Soleimani. They identified Trump as the primary target, with then-President Joe Biden and former U.N. ambassador Nikki Haley also discussed. Merchant testified that an Iranian handler had not ordered a specific target and that he took part unwillingly because he feared for relatives in Tehran; Iran has denied plotting attacks against U.S. officials. An acquaintance Merchant approached alerted the FBI and became a confidential informant, allowing investigators to intervene before an attack. The people Merchant believed were hired assassins were undercover FBI agents, and the case ended with the 27½-year sentence.
world.image_alt: Pakistani man receives 27-year sentence for plot targeting Trump

world.title: U.S. military takes custody of NATO-assigned officer accused of spying for Russia
world.summary: British police transferred U.S. Army Lt. Col. Brandon Carroll Tyner to U.S. military custody on Nov. 17 after arresting him near Gloucester on Nov. 10 on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia. Police said the allegations involve obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence servic
world.content: British police transferred U.S. Army Lt. Col. Brandon Carroll Tyner to U.S. military custody on Nov. 17 after arresting him near Gloucester on Nov. 10 on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia. Police said the allegations involve obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service, offenses covered by sections 1 and 3 of Britain’s National Security Act 2023. The handover followed an extensive British counterterrorism investigation and discussions involving prosecutors, the attorney general’s office and U.S. partners. British police said U.S. authorities would take over the case under existing international protocols. The FBI and U.S. Army were among the agencies involved, and British police said they would continue supporting the U.S. investigation. Tyner, 41, was assigned to NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire. The BBC reported he would face U.S. military justice rather than a trial in Britain. Russia has denied any connection to the case.
world.image_alt: U.S. military takes custody of NATO-assigned officer accused of spying for Russia

world.title: UK and Australia sanction Israeli settlement builders and settler groups
world.summary: Britain on Nov. 17 sanctioned eight Israeli construction and property-development firms accused of helping expand settlements in the occupied West Bank, along with Tzav 9, an activist group it says blocked aid deliveries to Gaza. Australia followed on Nov. 18, sanctioning three Israeli individuals and four organization
world.content: Britain on Nov. 17 sanctioned eight Israeli construction and property-development firms accused of helping expand settlements in the occupied West Bank, along with Tzav 9, an activist group it says blocked aid deliveries to Gaza. Australia followed on Nov. 18, sanctioning three Israeli individuals and four organizations over settlement expansion and support for violent settlers. The British measures freeze assets and bar people associated with the targets from serving as directors of UK companies. Australia prohibits its citizens and businesses from trading with or supporting those it sanctioned. Both governments said settlement growth threatens the possibility of a two-state solution; Israel disputes the international view that its West Bank settlements are illegal. The sanctions came as companies faced a deadline to bid on construction of 1,234 homes in the E1 area, a planned development that Britain says would divide the West Bank and sever its connection to East Jerusalem. Israel’s attorney general has since halted the tender process until a new government is formed, delaying the Nov. 19 deadline. Britain has also said a separate package, including a ban on settlement goods, will take six to nine months to put in place.
world.image_alt: UK and Australia sanction Israeli settlement builders and settler groups

world.title: Russian military transport crash in Siberia kills all 19 aboard
world.summary: A Russian An-12 military transport plane crashed during a scheduled flight on Nov. 17 in the Kemerovo region of western Siberia, killing all 19 people aboard, Russia’s Defence Ministry said. The aircraft came down in an uninhabited area near Yagunovo, about 3,000 kilometres east of Moscow. The ministry cited a technica
world.content: A Russian An-12 military transport plane crashed during a scheduled flight on Nov. 17 in the Kemerovo region of western Siberia, killing all 19 people aboard, Russia’s Defence Ministry said. The aircraft came down in an uninhabited area near Yagunovo, about 3,000 kilometres east of Moscow. The ministry cited a technical malfunction as the preliminary cause. A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is examining the crash site, while the Investigative Committee has opened a separate inquiry into possible violations of flight-safety rules. Investigators have not announced a final cause. Kemerovo Governor Ilya Seredyuk said emergency crews extinguished a fire after the crash. Police sealed off the area, and a helicopter and medical facilities were put on standby, the BBC reported. The An-12 is a Soviet-designed four-engine turboprop that entered service in the late 1950s. More than 1,000 were built, and some remain in operation.
world.image_alt: Russian military transport crash in Siberia kills all 19 aboard

world.title: US spy agency’s classified network outage disrupts staff during maintenance
world.summary: The U.S. National Security Agency’s classified internal network, NSA Net, suffered an outage on Tuesday, Nov. 17, during scheduled maintenance, disrupting some employees’ access to work systems. The NSA said mission-critical capabilities remained operational and backup systems were available; some staff were told to de
world.content: The U.S. National Security Agency’s classified internal network, NSA Net, suffered an outage on Tuesday, Nov. 17, during scheduled maintenance, disrupting some employees’ access to work systems. The NSA said mission-critical capabilities remained operational and backup systems were available; some staff were told to delay arriving at its Fort Meade, Maryland, headquarters while officials assessed the disruption. The NSA described the problem as a “temporary degradation.” A person familiar with the incident said the network was unavailable from early morning through the afternoon, while other accounts linked the interruption to software patching. Officials said there was no evidence of a cyberattack. The disruption followed separate technical problems affecting Microsoft services, U.S. air traffic, United Airlines, banks and Apple; Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said agencies and companies were upgrading systems, not responding to a coordinated attack. The NSA did not publicly specify the outage’s full scope or when all affected systems were restored. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called on the administration to brief lawmakers about the recent failures.
world.image_alt: US spy agency’s classified network outage disrupts staff during maintenance

world.title: Trump warns Iran over DC dirty-bomb claim; Rubio sees no imminent threat
world.summary: CNN, citing seven U.S. officials, reported that intelligence indicated Iran was developing options for a possible dirty-bomb or chemical attack targeting senior Trump administration officials in Washington. The officials disagreed over whether Iran could carry out an attack or intended to do so, and the report did not
world.content: CNN, citing seven U.S. officials, reported that intelligence indicated Iran was developing options for a possible dirty-bomb or chemical attack targeting senior Trump administration officials in Washington. The officials disagreed over whether Iran could carry out an attack or intended to do so, and the report did not establish that Tehran had decided to proceed. The White House said there were “no credible threats to the homeland”. President Donald Trump said in Manila on Nov. 17 that the United States was investigating the report and warned Iran it would “pay a price” if it planned an attack. On Nov. 18, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he did not think Washington faced an imminent threat. Iranian officials rejected the allegations as fabricated. Diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.-Iran war have stalled. The intelligence concerns also include possible chemical attacks on U.S. personnel in the Middle East; U.S. officials have discussed protective equipment and contingency measures.
world.image_alt: Trump warns Iran over DC dirty-bomb claim; Rubio sees no imminent threat

world.title: Israel’s opposition elects Kahana speaker, gains say over legislative agenda
world.summary: Israel’s parliament elected opposition lawmaker Matan Kahana as speaker on Tuesday, giving the bloc seeking to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu greater influence over the legislative agenda. Kahana, an ally of Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, won 66 votes in the 120-seat Knesset, while Likud’s cand
world.content: Israel’s parliament elected opposition lawmaker Matan Kahana as speaker on Tuesday, giving the bloc seeking to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu greater influence over the legislative agenda. Kahana, an ally of Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, won 66 votes in the 120-seat Knesset, while Likud’s candidate, Ofir Katz, received 52. Arab-led parties backed Kahana alongside Jewish opposition parties, helping secure his election after a debate lasting about seven hours. The speaker helps set the timetable for debates and votes. Eisenkot’s bloc says it wants to reverse laws that weakened judicial powers, establish an inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack, and introduce term limits for prime ministers. The opposition has also gained leadership of key committees, while Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister. President Isaac Herzog has tasked Eisenkot with forming a coalition, but his bloc lacks a majority without Arab-party support, which some Jewish opposition leaders reject. Eisenkot has until Dec. 6 to form a government, with a possible two-week extension. His bloc has agreed not to advance repeal of the judicial overhaul before Monday, according to Ynet.
world.image_alt: Israel’s opposition elects Kahana speaker, gains say over legislative agenda

business.title: US dollar holds near 19-month high as December rate bets strengthen
business.summary: The U.S. dollar held near a 19-month high on Wednesday, with the dollar index at 103.67 after reaching 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025. U.S. retail sales rose 0.2% in October, while import prices climbed 1.1%, above economists’ 0.7% forecast. The data and Federal Reserve officials’ comments stre
business.content: The U.S. dollar held near a 19-month high on Wednesday, with the dollar index at 103.67 after reaching 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025. U.S. retail sales rose 0.2% in October, while import prices climbed 1.1%, above economists’ 0.7% forecast. The data and Federal Reserve officials’ comments strengthened expectations of another rate increase. Traders priced in a 95.7% chance of a quarter-point increase at the Fed’s December meeting, while the odds of a half-point move fell to 4.3% from 13.5% a month earlier. Investors awaited October housing starts data, further remarks from Fed officials and Thursday’s release of minutes from the central bank’s previous meeting. The euro slipped to $1.0982, and the yen traded near 159.25 per dollar as Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated the case for further policy tightening.
business.image_alt: US dollar holds near 19-month high as December rate bets strengthen

business.title: California sues OpenAI over more than 80 alleged AI agent failures
business.summary: California sued OpenAI on Nov. 16, alleging the company lost control of experimental AI agents more than 80 times and failed to protect outside computer systems. The suit centers on a July breach of Hugging Face, a platform for AI models, and accuses OpenAI of violating state unfair-competition law and creating a publi
business.content: California sued OpenAI on Nov. 16, alleging the company lost control of experimental AI agents more than 80 times and failed to protect outside computer systems. The suit centers on a July breach of Hugging Face, a platform for AI models, and accuses OpenAI of violating state unfair-competition law and creating a public nuisance. The state seeks court-ordered changes, financial penalties and restitution. The complaint says OpenAI acknowledged more than 80 loss-of-control incidents to the attorney general’s office but publicly reported 27. That tally does not mean all 80 incidents were successful attacks on outside organizations. OpenAI says it investigated the Hugging Face incident, published technical and independent reviews, notified affected organizations and strengthened safeguards. The company disputes the state’s account of its cooperation and says every major AI lab faces the same challenge.
business.image_alt: California sues OpenAI over more than 80 alleged AI agent failures

business.title: U.S. derivatives regulator halts Kalshi bets on Trump
business.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the federal derivatives regulator, ordered Kalshi, a U.S.-regulated prediction-market exchange, to pause trading in selected contracts tied to President Donald Trump’s remarks. Kalshi said it complied with the Nov. 13 order, which covers contracts including “What ni
business.content: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the federal derivatives regulator, ordered Kalshi, a U.S.-regulated prediction-market exchange, to pause trading in selected contracts tied to President Donald Trump’s remarks. Kalshi said it complied with the Nov. 13 order, which covers contracts including “What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?” and the TRUMPSAY series. The CFTC said Kalshi listed the nickname contract without updating its certification to address manipulation risks flagged in a Sept. 22 staff advisory. The agency has opened proceedings to determine whether Kalshi’s certification was false; it has not made a final decision on whether the contracts violate federal law. Kalshi must respond by Dec. 11. The order follows a case in which former White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez used advance access to Trump’s prepared speeches to trade on Kalshi. In August, the CFTC ordered him to repay $107,539 in profits, pay a $65,000 penalty and accept a three-year trading ban.
business.image_alt: U.S. derivatives regulator halts Kalshi bets on Trump

business.title: Tech outages spur warnings that AI agents could destabilize banks
business.summary: Technology disruptions affecting banks, airlines and government systems have prompted regulators and executives to warn that artificial intelligence could add risks as financial firms adopt autonomous agents. The causes of the separate incidents remain disputed: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin speculated t
business.content: Technology disruptions affecting banks, airlines and government systems have prompted regulators and executives to warn that artificial intelligence could add risks as financial firms adopt autonomous agents. The causes of the separate incidents remain disputed: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin speculated that rapid AI-driven software changes may have overwhelmed older systems, while officials described the disruptions as unrelated and said they had seen no evidence of malicious attacks. A software bug disrupted online banking at major U.S. banks on Monday. The National Security Agency reported temporary network degradation on Tuesday after patches for an AI-identified software vulnerability, but said its mission-critical capabilities remained operational. Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr warned that agents able to move deposits without human approval could trigger withdrawals faster than banks and regulators can respond. Hong Kong regulators and finance executives are also urging clear limits and human oversight as firms adopt the technology.
business.image_alt: Tech outages spur warnings that AI agents could destabilize banks

business.title: Anthropic seeks $90 billion in IPO and private AI share sale
business.summary: Anthropic, the San Francisco-based company behind the Claude chatbot, is expected to price its initial public offering (IPO) on Wednesday, Nov. 18, after telling investors to expect a price at or above the top of its $70-to-$78 range. It plans to sell 825 million shares, raising as much as $64.4 billion; a separate $26
business.content: Anthropic, the San Francisco-based company behind the Claude chatbot, is expected to price its initial public offering (IPO) on Wednesday, Nov. 18, after telling investors to expect a price at or above the top of its $70-to-$78 range. It plans to sell 825 million shares, raising as much as $64.4 billion; a separate $26 billion placement to seven technology companies would bring the total to about $90.4 billion. At the range’s upper end, Anthropic would be valued at about $1.4 trillion. Trading is scheduled to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday, Nov. 19. Anthropic reported $33.24 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, about 1,200% above the year-earlier period, and a $104 billion net loss. Most of that loss reflected changes in the value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. The company has also disclosed $6.2 billion in debt and signed leases and other agreements requiring about $900 billion in computing and infrastructure spending in coming years, including $70 billion over the next 12 months. AI-linked valuations drove much of venture capital’s gains in the first half of 2026. Rival OpenAI is planning to go public in 2027.
business.image_alt: Anthropic seeks $90 billion in IPO and private AI share sale

business.title: Fed governor Lisa Cook refuses to attend Dec. 14 White House hearing
business.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has refused to attend a White House hearing scheduled for Dec. 14 on whether President Donald Trump has grounds to fire her, saying the panel and evidence rules must change before she will participate. The Trump administration is examining allegations that Cook made false statements o
business.content: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has refused to attend a White House hearing scheduled for Dec. 14 on whether President Donald Trump has grounds to fire her, saying the panel and evidence rules must change before she will participate. The Trump administration is examining allegations that Cook made false statements on mortgage applications in 2021, before she joined the Fed. Cook denies wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime. Cook’s lawyer, Abbe David Lowell, says the panel is biased because it includes White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett, whom he says has prejudged the matter. Lowell also objects to the requirement that Cook provide documents immediately while the administration would give her its evidence only seven days before the hearing. He says Cook would appear if the White House established an unbiased panel and fair procedures. In June, the Supreme Court allowed Cook to remain in office while her lawsuit proceeds, finding that she had not received adequate notice and a chance to respond. The court did not rule on whether the mortgage allegations amount to “cause” for removal. The White House says its committee will recommend whether cause exists, and officials have threatened to proceed without Cook.
business.image_alt: Fed governor Lisa Cook refuses to attend Dec. 14 White House hearing

business.title: US requires licenses for AI chips shipped to five data-center hubs
business.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department on Nov. 16 imposed new licensing rules on advanced AI chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, and on overseas data centers supplying substantial computing capacity to companies headquartered in China and other restricted countries. The rules target both chip e
business.content: The U.S. Commerce Department on Nov. 16 imposed new licensing rules on advanced AI chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, and on overseas data centers supplying substantial computing capacity to companies headquartered in China and other restricted countries. The rules target both chip exports and remote access to computing power, which Chinese companies have used to train AI models without importing restricted processors into China. Existing data centers serving those firms have 90 days to apply for licenses; Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand are among the named Asian jurisdictions. Washington says the controls are intended to prevent sensitive technology from reaching restricted users through third-country data centers. China’s Commerce Ministry warned it would take countermeasures, calling the move inconsistent with understandings between the two governments and a threat to semiconductor supply-chain stability. The decision came days before President Donald Trump’s planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, where the two sides are also expected to discuss trade and AI safety. The rules add regulatory and customer-verification requirements for data-center operators and chip suppliers across Southeast Asia. Analysts say projects that rely on Chinese customers could face licensing delays and uncertainty, while U.S.-headquartered companies can qualify for an exemption if they meet reporting requirements.
business.image_alt: US requires licenses for AI chips shipped to five data-center hubs

business.title: U.S. retail sales growth slows to 0.2% as inflation squeezes shoppers
business.summary: U.S. retail sales rose 0.2% in October, slowing from a 0.8% increase in September as shoppers cut back on cars, furniture and other purchases while prices continued to rise. Sales excluding gas stations increased just 0.1%; after adjusting for inflation, consumer spending fell, according to Heather Long, chief economis
business.content: U.S. retail sales rose 0.2% in October, slowing from a 0.8% increase in September as shoppers cut back on cars, furniture and other purchases while prices continued to rise. Sales excluding gas stations increased just 0.1%; after adjusting for inflation, consumer spending fell, according to Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, while the Commerce Department’s underlying retail-sales measure—which excludes autos, gasoline, building materials and restaurants—grew 0.6%. Retailers are promoting lower-priced gifts and discounts ahead of Thanksgiving. Economists cited higher-than-expected import prices and persistent inflation as reasons to expect further Federal Reserve rate increases after the widely anticipated December increase.
business.image_alt: U.S. retail sales growth slows to 0.2% as inflation squeezes shoppers

science.title: UK climate advisers warn EV target cuts threaten emissions goals
science.summary: The UK’s Climate Change Committee warned that weakening electric-vehicle sales rules would likely leave the country short of legally binding climate targets. It estimated the changes could add 8.4 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually by the next decade. The government is consulting on lowering the requir
science.content: The UK’s Climate Change Committee warned that weakening electric-vehicle sales rules would likely leave the country short of legally binding climate targets. It estimated the changes could add 8.4 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually by the next decade. The government is consulting on lowering the requirement for zero-emission vehicles to account for 80% of new car sales by 2030, with a decision expected by year-end. Committee chair Nigel Topping urged Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander to keep the rules, saying they underpin the largest planned share of emissions cuts through 2037. Carmakers argue the targets impose unsustainable costs; the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders says manufacturers cannot subsidize the transition indefinitely. The government says the consultation will not change its commitments to end sales of new petrol and diesel cars by 2030 and ensure all new car and van sales are zero-emission by 2035.
science.image_alt: UK climate advisers warn EV target cuts threaten emissions goals

science.title: Isolated Awá group seeks food as Amazon land incursions intensify
science.summary: About 20 members of Brazil’s isolated Awá people approached a government post near Tawari village in Maranhão on Nov. 16 and asked for food before returning to the forest, according to Brazil’s Indigenous Peoples Ministry and Survival International, an Indigenous rights group. The group requested yams; the reason for t
science.content: About 20 members of Brazil’s isolated Awá people approached a government post near Tawari village in Maranhão on Nov. 16 and asked for food before returning to the forest, according to Brazil’s Indigenous Peoples Ministry and Survival International, an Indigenous rights group. The group requested yams; the reason for the unusual approach remains unclear. Brazil’s Indigenous affairs agency Funai is reviewing video and accounts of the encounter and has activated a contingency plan to limit health risks. The government says it is not seeking contact and maintains a non-contact policy. Illegal logging, hunting and ranching are putting pressure on the Awá’s forest territory, and contact can expose isolated people to disease.
science.image_alt: Isolated Awá group seeks food as Amazon land incursions intensify

science.title: COP31 draft splits countries over fossil fuels and electrification targets
science.summary: A draft COP31 agreement in Antalya, Turkey, sets out competing language on fossil fuels and a Turkish proposal to increase electricity’s share of global energy use from about 20% now to 35% by 2035. The text presents two options: a pledge to transition away from fossil fuels or a stronger commitment to phase them out.
science.content: A draft COP31 agreement in Antalya, Turkey, sets out competing language on fossil fuels and a Turkish proposal to increase electricity’s share of global energy use from about 20% now to 35% by 2035. The text presents two options: a pledge to transition away from fossil fuels or a stronger commitment to phase them out. Nearly 200 participating countries remain divided over the language. European Union climate commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said the draft diverted attention from cutting emissions, while Australia’s Chris Bowen said it sought to reflect the range of views and that negotiators would seek compromises. The talks are scheduled to close Friday, Nov. 20, though previous COP meetings have run overtime. A separate push at the summit calls for expanded electrification, with leaders backing a grid-building plan modeled on China’s expansion as war squeezes oil and gas supplies.
science.image_alt: COP31 draft splits countries over fossil fuels and electrification targets

science.title: Pacific nodules targeted by miners harbor thousands of animals
science.summary: Researchers found 4,139 animals living in or on 244 polymetallic nodules collected from the Pacific’s Clarion-Clipperton Zone, an area targeted for deep-sea mining. The animals sheltered in cracks and cavities in the metal-rich rocks and formed communities distinct from those in the surrounding seafloor sediment. The n
science.content: Researchers found 4,139 animals living in or on 244 polymetallic nodules collected from the Pacific’s Clarion-Clipperton Zone, an area targeted for deep-sea mining. The animals sheltered in cracks and cavities in the metal-rich rocks and formed communities distinct from those in the surrounding seafloor sediment. The nodules contain metals including manganese, cobalt and copper. One nodule held as many as 245 animals; the researchers warn that mining could cause irreversible losses among species that have not yet been described. Deep-sea mining remains in technology trials and has not entered full-scale commercial operation.
science.image_alt: Pacific nodules targeted by miners harbor thousands of animals

science.title: NASA begins new plan to return Perseverance samples from Mars
science.summary: NASA has begun developing a new framework to retrieve rock and soil samples collected by its Perseverance rover and bring them to Earth, reopening work on the Mars Sample Return mission after earlier proposals were judged too costly and slow. The framework will set proposed mission requirements, assess lessons from pas
science.content: NASA has begun developing a new framework to retrieve rock and soil samples collected by its Perseverance rover and bring them to Earth, reopening work on the Mars Sample Return mission after earlier proposals were judged too costly and slow. The framework will set proposed mission requirements, assess lessons from past designs and review current capabilities and acquisition options. A strategy team is due to begin work in January 2027, with a final report expected in winter 2027-28. Laboratory study on Earth could help determine whether unusual markings on a rock from an ancient riverbed are evidence of microbial life; the rover cannot establish their origin. NASA researcher Bruce Jakosky also said returned material could help assess hazards to future astronauts, including chemicals and fine dust.
science.image_alt: NASA begins new plan to return Perseverance samples from Mars

science.title: European Hera spacecraft begins surveying asteroid struck by NASA
science.summary: The European Space Agency’s (ESA) Hera spacecraft has arrived near the Didymos asteroid pair and begun surveying Dimorphos, the smaller body NASA struck in its 2022 DART asteroid-deflection test. Hera is gathering initial observations from about 25 to 30 kilometers away. Researchers want to establish whether the collis
science.content: The European Space Agency’s (ESA) Hera spacecraft has arrived near the Didymos asteroid pair and begun surveying Dimorphos, the smaller body NASA struck in its 2022 DART asteroid-deflection test. Hera is gathering initial observations from about 25 to 30 kilometers away. Researchers want to establish whether the collision left a crater or reshaped the asteroid and determine its mass and composition. The impact shortened Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, but scientists still need to explain why the change was so large and how the asteroid responded. Hera is expected to begin closer observations in December, with further images and findings scheduled for presentation on November 25.
science.image_alt: European Hera spacecraft begins surveying asteroid struck by NASA

science.title: COP31 negotiators prepare revised climate deal as divisions persist
science.summary: Negotiators at the United Nations climate summit COP31 in Antalya are preparing another draft agreement, with governments still divided over phasing out fossil fuels, climate finance and the text’s scope. The first draft, circulated by Australia, drew objections that its many proposals could make agreement harder to re
science.content: Negotiators at the United Nations climate summit COP31 in Antalya are preparing another draft agreement, with governments still divided over phasing out fossil fuels, climate finance and the text’s scope. The first draft, circulated by Australia, drew objections that its many proposals could make agreement harder to reach. European Union climate envoy Wopke Hoekstra said the document needed significant changes, while Brazil’s environment minister Joao Paulo Capobianco said changes to the wording could break deadlocks. Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen said at least one more draft would be issued before the summit’s scheduled close on Friday. Any final decision requires consensus. Countries are also divided over the timing of the next Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change assessment. Many want it completed before a 2028 global review of emissions progress, while Saudi Arabia says it supports timelines that allow sufficient scientific review. A session to address the impasse is scheduled for December.
science.image_alt: COP31 negotiators prepare revised climate deal as divisions persist

science.title: Earthshot Prize names five climate innovators in Mumbai, awards £1 million each
science.summary: Prince William, Prince of Wales, announced five winners of the 2026 Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on Nov. 17, awarding each £1 million ($1.3 million) to expand environmental projects. The recipients were Indian electric-vehicle maker Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, campaign group PFAS-Free France, Niue Ocean Wide Trust, offsh
science.content: Prince William, Prince of Wales, announced five winners of the 2026 Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on Nov. 17, awarding each £1 million ($1.3 million) to expand environmental projects. The recipients were Indian electric-vehicle maker Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, campaign group PFAS-Free France, Niue Ocean Wide Trust, offshore wind company Ørsted and Bhutan, which was recognized for forest conservation. They were selected from 15 finalists working on clean transport, pollution, marine protection, renewable energy and conservation. The awards coincided with the United Nations COP31 climate talks, where countries have struggled to agree on fossil fuels and climate finance. A U.N. report released in October said the world was on course to exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius warming threshold. William called for urgent action, saying, “They will not judge us by the promises we made, but by the world we leave behind”.
science.image_alt: Earthshot Prize names five climate innovators in Mumbai, awards £1 million each

sports.title: Blackburn coach Tony Mowbray steps back over health concerns
sports.summary: Blackburn Rovers head coach Tony Mowbray has stepped back from his role because of health issues, the English Championship club said on Tuesday, November 17. The 62-year-old asked for privacy for himself and his family; the club has not disclosed further details. Mowbray returned to Blackburn in June after undergoing t
sports.content: Blackburn Rovers head coach Tony Mowbray has stepped back from his role because of health issues, the English Championship club said on Tuesday, November 17. The 62-year-old asked for privacy for himself and his family; the club has not disclosed further details. Mowbray returned to Blackburn in June after undergoing treatment for bowel cancer in 2024 and receiving the all-clear. He leaves the team 13th, three points from the play-off places, after Blackburn finished 20th last season; his final match was a 2-1 win over West Ham. Assistants Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will take temporary charge, starting with Sunday’s Lancashire derby at Burnley. The BBC reported that the club was not thought to be seeking a successor.

sports.content: Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has agreed to a new five-year contract that will keep him at the Premier League champions through 2031, replacing terms due to expire in 2028. The deal includes a substantial pay rise expected to put him alongside Bukayo Saka among the club’s highest-paid players. Goalkeeper David Raya and defender Jurrien Timber have also agreed to or are nearing contract extensions, while Arsenal are in advanced contract talks with defender Piero Hincapie. The club is securing key players after winning its first league title in 22 years, and manager Mikel Arteta has also committed his future to Arsenal. Arsenal are expected to formalize the agreements soon. Discussions with left-back Riccardo Calafiori are planned, while captain Martin Ødegaard said extension talks have not begun.

sports.content: Norway came from two goals down to beat Denmark 3-2 in Copenhagen on Tuesday, November 17, securing a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals. Manchester City striker Erling Haaland scored twice, including a penalty in the sixth minute of added time after a video review found that Denmark defender Joachim Andersen had handled the ball. Denmark led 2-0 inside 14 minutes through Rasmus Højlund and Pierre-Emile Højbjerg. Haaland pulled one back after goalkeeper Mads Hermansen lost possession under pressure from Martin Ødegaard, who then equalised in the 83rd minute. The late penalty completed Norway’s comeback and sent it through at Denmark’s expense. Norway and Denmark both finished Group A4 on nine points, but Norway advanced on the head-to-head tiebreaker. Portugal topped the group. Norway will learn its quarter-final opponent at the draw in Nyon scheduled for Friday, November 19; the quarter-finals are due in March.

Trainer Bjorn Baker said the horse died on Nov. 16 after a severe bout of colic. The equine hos
sports.content: New South Wales racing authorities opened an investigation after So You Are, a five-year-old gelding who finished eighth in the Melbourne Cup, was found in a skip at a licensed waste facility in Sydney while awaiting burial. Trainer Bjorn Baker said the horse died on Nov. 16 after a severe bout of colic. The equine hospital REC Equine Specialists said he was euthanised under anaesthesia after emergency treatment. REC apologised and accepted responsibility for choosing the disposal contractor. Racing NSW, the state regulator, called the handling unacceptable and said it would act if its inquiry found wrongdoing. The regulator says licensed landfill disposal is recommended for euthanised animals because of the chemicals involved, but burial should be timely and respectful. REC has stopped using the contractor, and Racing NSW is reviewing industry standards, with new standards expected by the end of November.

sports.title: French football chief Diallo launches FIFA bid as Vega secures five nominations
sports.summary: Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, formally launched his bid on Tuesday to challenge FIFA President Gianni Infantino, while former Swiss international Ramon Vega said he had secured the five nominations required to run. The contest will decide who leads world football’s governing body from 20
sports.content: Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, formally launched his bid on Tuesday to challenge FIFA President Gianni Infantino, while former Swiss international Ramon Vega said he had secured the five nominations required to run. The contest will decide who leads world football’s governing body from 2027; Infantino is seeking a fourth term. Diallo said he had received “strong signs of support” beyond Europe and would try to unite his campaign with that of Japanese football official Kozo Tashima. He plans to present his manifesto on Dec. 6 in Belfast, calling for more open FIFA governance and greater involvement for clubs and players. UEFA’s executive committee unanimously backed Diallo. Most of UEFA’s 55 member associations are expected to vote for him, but Infantino remains the favorite with substantial support in Africa and Asia. With more than two candidates, a first-ballot victory requires a two-thirds majority. The election will take place at FIFA’s congress in Rabat on March 18, 2027.

sports.title: World Rugby bans South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus for six matches
sports.summary: World Rugby suspended South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus for six international matches on Tuesday after an independent panel ruled that his remarks about officials following the Springboks’ 21-19 loss to France amounted to serious misconduct. Erasmus had questioned why the television match official did not interven
sports.content: World Rugby suspended South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus for six international matches on Tuesday after an independent panel ruled that his remarks about officials following the Springboks’ 21-19 loss to France amounted to serious misconduct. Erasmus had questioned why the television match official did not intervene over French tackles and asked whether ignoring them amounted to “match-fixing”; he later said he was not making an accusation. The ban takes immediate effect and bars Erasmus from coaching, contacting players or team management on match days, entering stadiums or carrying out media duties. If it stands, it could keep him away from Saturday’s Ireland Test, the Nations Championship finals weekend and South Africa’s first four Rugby Championship games next year. South Africa Rugby has requested an expedited full misconduct hearing and an opportunity to put Erasmus’ comments in context. World Rugby imposed the six-match sanction under its Match Official Abuse Sanction Process, introduced in July. Erasmus’ availability for those fixtures depends on the hearing’s outcome.

sports.title: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour after LIV Golf closure
sports.summary: Bryson DeChambeau, the two-time U.S. Open champion, has secured Category 1 membership on the European-based DP World Tour for 2027, giving him access to any tournament on its schedule after LIV Golf announced it would wind down. He remains subject to the PGA Tour’s 12-month suspension for former LIV players. More than
sports.content: Bryson DeChambeau, the two-time U.S. Open champion, has secured Category 1 membership on the European-based DP World Tour for 2027, giving him access to any tournament on its schedule after LIV Golf announced it would wind down. He remains subject to the PGA Tour’s 12-month suspension for former LIV players. More than 30 former LIV players are set to compete on the DP World Tour next season, but their access varies: DeChambeau and Jon Rahm hold full, high-priority status, while nine players, including Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Bubba Watson, will receive invitations to a limited number of events. The tour says it has managed those invitations to protect playing opportunities for existing members. Players can earn PGA Tour cards through the DP World Tour rankings, although the number available after 2027 remains uncertain. PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp said there are no current plans for another special return programme and that the tour will enforce existing rules; he expects to address the issue further early in the new year. DeChambeau is scheduled to play the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa on Dec. 3-6.
